title: dynamic-shot-allocation-and-context-slicing-guide-2026
author: Priya Menon
body:
Title: Dynamic Shot Allocation and Context Slicing — Guide for Evaluations and Model Onboarding

Summary
-------
This guide explains a standardized approach to:

- Allocating few-shot examples dynamically per request during evaluation and onboarding
- Slicing long-context inputs into coherent segments for benchmarking and production stress tests
- Measuring stability and sensitivity across shot counts and slice strategies (useful for quantization experiments, regression triage, and prompt robustness)

Goals
-----
1. Reduce noise when comparing model variants by controlling shot distribution and slice semantics.
2. Provide repeatable, automated recipes for per-workload shot selection so evals reflect real-world prompt distributions.
3. Define a triage path when quality regressions correlate with shot or slice behavior.

When to use this guide
----------------------
Use for:
- Model onboarding (certification) when comparing a new model vs baseline across variable context budgets.
- Benchmarking long-context and cache-sensitive workloads.
- Investigations where output quality diverges between few-shot and zero-shot regimes.

Definitions
-----------
- Dynamic shot allocation (DSA): algorithmic selection of example seeds per request based on metadata (intent, entity types, complexity).
- Context slice: contiguous or semantic chunk of a long document passed as prompt context.
- Slice policy: rules that determine overlap, size, and boundary alignment (token or semantic).

Recommended patterns
--------------------
1. Metadata-driven sampling: attach labels to prompt candidates (intent, domain, length bucket) and sample shots to match target distribution.
2. Adaptive budgeting: if token budget is constrained, prefer example diversity over raw count (i.e., 3 diverse shots > 5 near-duplicate shots).
3. Semantic boundary slicing: prefer sentence/paragraph boundaries; fall back to token-based slices for highly fragmented content.

Configuration table (recommended defaults)
----------------------------------------
| Config | Default | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| max_context_tokens | 8192 | Matches common long-context models we evaluate |
| default_shot_counts | [0, 1, 3, 8] | Sweep these during cert to capture zero/low/medium/high regimes |
| slice_size_tokens | 512 | Balance between coherence and throughput |
| slice_overlap_tokens | 40 | Small overlap keeps context continuity for coreference |
| selection_strategy | metadata-weighted-random | Robust across skewed prompt catalogs |

Step-by-step: creating a DSA + slicing eval suite
------------------------------------------------
1. Define workload partitions: label the prompt corpus with intent/domain/length bucket.
2. Choose shot policies per partition: e.g., customer-support -> [3,8], semantic-search-snippets -> [0,1].
3. Implement slice policy: semantic-first -> paragraph align -> 512-token max -> 40-token overlap.
4. Generate evaluation variants: for each model-version create permutations across shot counts and slice strategies.
5. Run parallel serving-simulation (see related serving-simulation-eval-harness) to include runtime effects like KV cache and batching.
6. Aggregate metrics: quality (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/accuracy/qa-f1), latency P95, and token-cost delta vs baseline.
7. Apply stability criteria (see "Decision thresholds").

Decision thresholds and pass/fail criteria
----------------------------------------
- Quality regression: >5% relative drop on primary metric for 3+ partitions flagged -> FAIL.
- Shot sensitivity: if metric delta between any two shot counts >6% and inconsistent direction across partitions -> mark "shot-unstable".
- Slice sensitivity: variance across slice strategies >7% absolute on primary metric -> requires triage.

Triage playbook for shot/slice regressions
-----------------------------------------
1. Reproduce: rerun failing partition with deterministic seed and fixed selection_strategy.
2. Isolate variables: run zero-shot, then single-shot, compare outputs to identify error modes (hallucination, truncation, formatting).
3. Run quantization profile variants (fp16, q4_0, q8_0) against the same slices to check if regressions are quantization-related.
4. Inspect KV cache behavior: use the serving runtime profiler to confirm cache hits/misses for repeated slices.
5. Collect minimally sufficient artifact bundle: failing prompts, model config, quantization profile, runtime logs, and sample outputs.
6. Open a regression ticket with label "shot-slice-regression" and attach artifacts. Assign to model-onboarding and runtime teams.

Example: CLI generator for slicing and shot sampling
---------------------------------------------------
```bash
# create variants with 0/1/3 shots and paragraph slicing
redwood-eval generate-variants \\  --input prompts.jsonl \\  --slice-policy paragraph:512:40 \\  --shots 0,1,3 \\  --metadata-key intent \\  --out variants/
```

JSON snippet: selection strategy proto
-------------------------------------
```json
{
  "selection_strategy": "metadata-weighted-random",
  "weights": {"billing": 0.5, "signup": 0.2, "troubleshooting": 0.3},
  "fallback": "uniform"
}
```

Practical notes and anti-patterns
--------------------------------
- Do: include at least one low-shot variant (1 shot) in all cert runs; many regressions manifest only at low shots.
- Do: keep example pools small (20–200 per partition) and curated for diversity.
- Don’t: rely solely on token-length slicing; semantic boundaries reduce spurious coreference failures.
- Don’t: run slice strategies without checking runtime cache behavior — overlapping slices can create cache churn and latency spikes.

Ownership, rollout, and automation
--------------------------------
- Owners: Applied ML (eval harness) for implementation; Model Onboarding for certification criteria; Serving Runtime for KV/cache metrics.
- Automation: add DSA+slice permutation generation to CI nightly runs for models under active development.
- Visibility: publish per-model "shot-slice stability" badges in model onboarding dashboards (green/orange/red).

Evaluation checklist (before cert sign-off)
-----------------------------------------
- [ ] All workload partitions exercised with 0/1/3/8 shots
- [ ] Slice strategies: paragraph, token-512, headline-priority tested
- [ ] Reproducible scripts and seeds committed to repo
- [ ] Artifacts uploaded to evaluation artifact store with manifest
- [ ] Quantization sensitivity report included (q4_0, q8_0)

Appendix: short checklist for SRE/Runtime when executing slices
-------------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm token budget and queueing policy for long slices.
2. Check KV cache telemetry to ensure repeated slices hit the cache (hit rate > 70%).
3. Monitor latency P95; if slice overlap causes P95 > baseline + 30% open a performance incident.
